title: Severe Airway Obstruction / Choking
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid Guidelines 2020; European Resuscitation Council (ERC) Guidelines for Resuscitation 2021

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately if the person cannot speak, cough forcefully, or breathe
If the person is coughing effectively, encourage them to keep coughing and do not interfere
If severe obstruction (silent struggle, clutching throat, inability to breathe): stand to the side and slightly behind, support their chest with one hand, and lean them forward
Deliver up to 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades using the heel of your other hand

If back blows fail to dislodge the object: stand behind, place a fist just above the navel (below ribcage), grasp fist with other hand, and pull sharply inwards and upwards (abdominal thrusts) up to 5 times
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the obstruction clears or emergency help arrives
If the person becomes unconscious: lower them carefully to the floor and begin CPR chest compressions immediately

do_not: Do not perform blind finger sweeps in the mouth; only remove a foreign object if it is clearly visible and easily grasped
Do not give oral fluids or food while the person is choking
Do not perform abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year old (use back blows and chest thrusts only)
